item.title: Welsh band shares streaming royalty data highlighting low Spotify pay-outs
item.description: Welsh indie rock band Los Campesinos! have publicly disclosed detailed streaming royalty figures from their 2024 album All Hell, offering a rare insight into the scale of per-stream pay-outs for independent artists and highlighting significant disparities between major digital platforms. The band released the data following widespread sharing of Spotify Wrapped statistics on social media in 2025. item.title: YouTube cracks down on fake trailer channels amid growing AI music concerns
item.description: YouTube has reportedly begun terminating channels responsible for unauthorised artificial intelligence-generated film trailers, raising questions about whether similar enforcement could soon extend to AI-generated music content. item.title: Hackers access Spotify music library, expose 256m tracks
item.description: Spotify has confirmed a security breach after hackers claimed to have scraped the platform’s entire music library, including metadata for 256 million tracks and profiles of over 15.4 million artists. The perpetrators, identifying themselves as part of a “non-profit project” called Anna’s Archive, stated that they had also accessed around 86 million audio files, representing almost 99.6% of all Spotify streams. item.title: BMG renews TikTok publishing deal, strengthens songwriter credits
item.description: Bertelsmann Music Group (BMG) has renewed its direct music publishing agreement with TikTok, extending a global partnership that includes new provisions aimed at improving songwriter crediting and data transparency on the video-sharing platform. Under the updated agreement, BMG will receive expanded reporting and attribution standards, alongside additional access to platform-level data to monitor how its publishing catalogue is used across TikTok. item.title: Global music copyright value hits record $47.2bn as growth slows
item.description: The global value of music copyright rose to a record $47.2 billion in 2024, according to a new report by music economist Will Page, marking a slowdown in growth as the industry moves beyond the pandemic-era rebound. The figure, published by Page on his Pivotal Economics platform, represents a 5.2% increase, or $2.3 billion, on the previous year. item.title: Apple Music offers three-month trial to PlayStation Plus members
item.description: Apple Music has partnered with Sony to offer PlayStation Plus subscribers up to three months of free access to its streaming service, as part of a late-year effort to attract new users. The offer is available to PlayStation Plus members who do not currently have an active Apple Music subscription. Eligibility also depends on a user’s subscription history, with some returning subscribers reporting that the trial is discounted rather than fully free. item.title: Bandcamp Fridays pay out $154m to artists since 2020
item.description: Direct-to-fan platform Bandcamp has paid out a total of $154 million to artists and labels through its Bandcamp Friday initiative since the programme launched in March 2020, according to figures released by the company. Bandcamp Fridays were introduced during the COVID-19 pandemic, when lockdowns severely reduced income from live performances and touring. item.title: Sound Stock launches 10 million-asset AI-curated royalty-free audio library
item.description: Sound Stock has launched a new royalty-free audio platform, positioning itself as the largest AI-cultivated library of original sound assets, with more than 10 million items available at launch. The company enters a competitive stock audio market with a model that combines in-house production, AI-assisted curation and a subscription structure designed to remove limits on access and downloads. The catalogue covers four main asset types including sound effects, samples, loops and full music tracks
